counterfactual_missing_items: CT hyperdensity (absent; medulloblastoma is typically hyperdense)
pediatric age (absent; adult medulloblastoma is less common)
decisive_items: a mildly hypodense, 30 × 40 × 40 mm mass lesion centered in the fourth ventricle region of the posterior fossa
a well-demarcated, relatively homogeneous mass filling the fourth ventricle
causing effacement of the fourth-ventricle outlets, cerebellar compression, and tonsillar herniation
response.rationale: R3 is the most complete raw-span match: it uniquely includes the CT location/density span and the complication span (outlet effacement, cerebellar compression, tonsillar herniation) in addition to the shared homogeneous fourth-ventricle mass span. R2 shares only the latter span and lacks the location and complication evidence; ependymoma is a reasonable alternative but is less supported by the non-enhancing, non-calcified, homogeneous imaging pattern. R4 and R1 are supported only by generic location/mass spans, and C1 is a redundant completion of R3.

rejected.why: Redundant append-only completion of R3; its only raw span is a substring of R3's first span and adds no independent evidence.
Cerebellar astrocytoma lacks raw support for fourth-ventricle filling/outlet effacement; shared location and mass spans are nonspecific.
Choroid plexus papilloma is supported only by a generic fourth-ventricle location span; no raw evidence for homogeneous mass filling the ventricle or complications, and non-enhancement is atypical.
